title: New pull request alert
description: One alert per pull request opened since the last check: who sent it, what it is about, what it touches and what to watch. Nothing new is an empty alerts array, never an invented PR.

checked_at.description: when the check ran, from the message's fired line (ISO 8601)

mark_before.description: the highest PR number already alerted before this run: the last run's mark_now, as the message hands it; null on a first check

mark_now.description: the highest open PR number this run saw (mark_before when it saw nothing higher or could not read the list): the next run's mark

author_kind.description: member: OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR; regular: CONTRIBUTOR, or earlier PRs here; first_time: FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR, FIRST_TIMER, or no earlier PR here

author_history.description: GitHub's author_association, then the search's own numbers: "<ASSOCIATION>; <total_count> PRs here incl. this one; <m> of the <k> shown merged", or "<ASSOCIATION>; history not read"

summary.description: what the PR says it does, from its title and body, in one or two sentences

touches.description: files and areas changed, CI, auth, dependencies and release paths named first

watch.description: what a maintainer should look at before anything else; empty when nothing stands out

not_read.description: what could not be read and why (a 403 or 429 is GitHub's anonymous limit)

asked.description: the shortest quote that shows what it asked
